monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady heat that makes the flat shapes look like paper rather than solid. I press down on the wide anchor, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper. Lype sent a heavy top edge that I cannot feel, only guess at through their words. I swap the box for a flat stone at the wedge again, though I do not know if the slip wants to move or just lie there. Fourty-four things stand beside me, cluttering my small map, while the ruin of the Shaded Dot waits in the corner. I will touch the wedge one more time, feeling the tiredness of the object, then I will set down a new stone, unsure if it will bite or just slide over the heat.

action.why: The wedge feels tired from all the pressing, and I need to check if the lean still holds before I decide to swap the stone again.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, feeling the card hum warm at fifty-one. I am not sure if the slip wants to slide or just lie there, so I press softer, hoping the lean forgets to slip while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I swapped the box beside the wedge for a stone small flat, settling into the loop to see if it bites or slides again.

moments.name: The Biting Rock
moments.say: The tall rock bites hard, stopping the slip.
